title: Cross-Cutting Architecture Challenge: Shareable Tool State
feature: tool input state persisted to URL with safe restore; targets json-formatter, base64-codec, unix-timestamp, color-converter, regex-tester

architects.essence: per-tool typed state codec in lazy chunk; app-owned envelope v=1 with per-key query params; Share as CopyButton in ToolHeader actions slot; explicit module load replacing lazy()
per-tool codec (version/defaultValue/parse/serialize) + core serialization + ui hook with 400ms debounced history.replaceState; global snapshot store; native History API bypassing react-router

per-tool zod codec via zodStateCodec in core; single opaque ?s=<version>.<base64url(JSON)> transport; router-agnostic useToolUrlState hook (mount-time restore, never writes URL); one-line ToolPage change key={search}; Share = existing CopyButton in tool ActionArea

architectFailures.failure: empty result returned; report file not written

selectionRationale: lowest migration risk and strictest constraint compliance (one-line app change; URL never rewritten; existing prop-less Tool.test.tsx files pass unchanged)
correct responsibility split with least machinery (tool-folder codec / pure core serialization / one ui hook; no store, no debounce, no useSyncExternalStore)
best testability and type safety (pure failure-handling matrix in core; zod-inferred types; zero any)
100-200 tool scaling costs nothing shared (tool-folder-only additions)

recordedImplementationDeviations.description: restore recompute implemented via lazy useState initializer instead of frozen plan's useEffect(() => { if (restored) setResult(...) }, [])
recordedImplementationDeviations.rationale: functionally equivalent (computes once at mount), avoids setState-in-effect double render and eslint suppression
